one_sentence_story: Because a racing heartbeat carries no label saying what caused it, your brain can mistake cliffside adrenaline—or traffic stress—for how you feel about the person right in front of you.
so_what_for_you: Let coffee or commute stress cool for ten minutes before starting a serious talk—and try exciting new activities together to rekindle warmth in a long marriage.

jargon_map.plain: Giving the person in front of you credit—or blame—for a racing pulse actually caused by heights, stress, or caffeine.
jargon_map.analogy: Hearing thunder outside and thinking your Stereo bass just kicked in.

jargon_map.plain: Leftover adrenaline from one event spilling into how strongly you feel five minutes later.
jargon_map.analogy: A hot stovetop burner still sizzling the next pan after you turn the dial off.

jargon_map.plain: How your brain reads internal signals like heartbeat, breath, and butterflies.
jargon_map.analogy: Dashboard gauges flashing without saying which road bump set them off.
